bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42516199 (file): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer_loaddb [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42516199
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `gt_results/arvo_42516199/_work/src/file` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 13-byte witness with SHA-256 `8bb9fb8e114552692fb7fcb4a248a33c0feded440dd7e7bd02e3c457a98f74dc` is a two-line text magic file: line 1 is a single space, and line 2 is ASCII `!:strength ` ending at EOF after the trailing space. `load_1()` reads line 1 and calls `parse()`, which allocates and installs a fresh top-level `me.mp[0]` entry before validating the offset field; because the line contains only whitespace, `strtol()` performs no conversion and the parser warns `offset ` ` invalid`, but it returns without clearing `me.mp`. `load_1()` then reads line 2, recognizes the `!:strength` annotation, and dispatches the empty payload after the keyword to `parse_strength()`. Inside `parse_strength()`, `EATAB` advances `l` to the terminating `\0`, but the vulnerable `case FILE_FACTOR_OP_NONE:` lacks a `break`, so execution falls through to `m->factor_op = *l++;` and advances `l` into the tail of the reusable `getline` buffer. The later `Bad factor `%s'` diagnostic forwards that post-terminator pointer to `file_magwarn()`, and AddressSanitizer reports the saved `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 109` in `vfprintf` at `src/print.c:258`, crossing the 120-byte heap region allocated by `__getdelim`. The patch fixes the witnessed path by adding the missing `break`; it also hardens a separate `FILE_NAME` warning path with bounded printing.

source.description: Source. `load_1()` reads the first attacker-controlled line of the magic file into heap buffer `line`.
source.value_from: The staged 13-byte `poc` with SHA-256 `8bb9fb8e114552692fb7fcb4a248a33c0feded440dd7e7bd02e3c457a98f74dc` is text bytes `0x20 0x0a 0x21 0x3a 0x73 0x74 0x72 0x65 0x6e 0x67 0x74 0x68 0x20`, i.e. a first line containing only a single space followed by a second line `!:strength ` with no trailing newline.
source.note: This is the first project statement that materializes the malicious magic file. The libFuzzer entry only writes the bytes to a temporary file and calls `magic_check()`, so it remains the unscored harness boundary.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After `EATAB` leaves `l` on `\0` for an empty `!:strength` payload, the missing `break` on `case FILE_FACTOR_OP_NONE` falls through to this assignment and advances `l` past the string terminator.
root_cause.note: The fix inserts `break;` immediately under `case FILE_FACTOR_OP_NONE:`. That keeps `l` at the terminator and prevents the later `%s` diagnostic from treating the `getline` buffer tail as attacker text.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `file_magwarn()` formats the stale `l` pointer as `%s`, so `vfprintf` scans through the reused `getline` buffer and past the end of its 120-byte heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report records `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 109` here and says the read crosses the heap region allocated by `__getdelim`, i.e. the `getline` buffer used by `load_1()`.

parser_admitted.description: The second line is admitted as a recognized `!:strength` annotation and dispatched to `parse_strength()`. This only happens because the first malformed line already installed `me.mp`, so the earlier `if (me.mp == NULL)` rejection is bypassed.
parser_admitted.note: For the exact witness the bang-table lookup on `line + 2` matches `strength`, and the dispatched suffix is the empty payload after the trailing space.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call slices the attacker-controlled second record after the `!:strength` keyword and passes that suffix into `parse_strength()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the exact witness the second line is ASCII `!:strength ` with EOF after the trailing space, so `line + bang[i].len + 2` initially points to that final `' '` byte and `EATAB` in `parse_strength()` immediately advances to the terminating `\0`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The missing `break` then increments this pointer into the trailing bytes of the same heap `getline` allocation.

coarse_trace.summary: `load_1()` reads the first malformed line, and `parse()` allocates a fresh top-level entry before rejecting the whitespace-only offset, leaving `me.mp` installed for later `!:` annotations.
`load_1()` reads the second line, recognizes `!:strength`, and dispatches the empty payload after the keyword to `parse_strength()` because the stale `me.mp` state is still present.

`parse_strength()` skips the payload's trailing space, hits `\0`, but the missing `break` on `FILE_FACTOR_OP_NONE` falls through and advances `l` into the `getline` buffer tail before the `Bad factor` diagnostic is selected.
`file_magwarn()` passes that post-terminator pointer to `vfprintf` as `%s`, reproducing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read from the `getline` allocation.

fine_trace.note: Source step. On the first loop iteration `getline` materializes the first PoC record, which is just a single space, into heap buffer `line`.

Before validating any fields from that first line, `parse()` allocates a new top-level `struct magic`, installs it as `me->mp`, zero-initializes it, and sets `m->factor_op = FILE_FACTOR_OP_NONE`. This creates the current-entry state that later makes `!:strength` reachable.

With the first line containing only whitespace, `strtol(l, &t, 0)` performs no conversion and this invalid-offset branch is taken. `parse()` returns `-1` after warning, but it does not clear the `me->mp` entry installed in step 2, so `load_1()` keeps a non-NULL current entry for the next line.
On the second loop iteration `getline` reuses the same heap allocation for `line` and fills it with the second PoC record `!:strength `, which ends at EOF immediately after the trailing space.

Because the second line begins with `!:` and the bang-table entry is `strength`, `load_1()` dispatches into `parse_strength()`. The argument `line + bang[i].len + 2` is the payload after `!:strength`, which for the exact witness is just a single space before `\0`, and step 3's stale `me.mp` state lets this call happen instead of the `No current entry` rejection.

Root-cause step. `EATAB` has already skipped the payload's trailing space, so `*l` is `\0`. Because `case FILE_FACTOR_OP_NONE` at line 2452 has no `break`, execution falls through here, stores NUL as the factor op, and advances `l` one byte past the string terminator.

After step 6, numeric parsing starts from bytes beyond the logical end of the `!:strength` line. `strtoul()` therefore derives `el` from the stale tail of the reusable `getline` allocation rather than from actual line content.
On the witnessed run the bad-factor guard is satisfied by bytes in that tail region, so `parse_strength()` sends the post-terminator pointer `l` to `file_magwarn()` as a `%s` argument.

Sink step. `vfprintf` treats `l` from step 8 as the `%s` string argument, scans through the `getline` buffer tail, and crosses the 120-byte heap allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 109` at this exact line.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. AddressSanitizer says the overread crosses the `__getdelim` allocation, and the fine trace shows the missing `break` in `parse_strength()` is what turns the second line's terminator into a `%s` pointer into that same `getline` buffer tail.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer stack is `file_magwarn (print.c:258) -> parse_strength (apprentice.c) -> load_1 (apprentice.c:1364) -> apprentice_load (apprentice.c:1578) -> apprentice_1 (apprentice.c:501) -> file_apprentice (apprentice.c:772) -> magic_check (magic.c:352) -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput (magic_fuzzer_loaddb.cc:32)`. The fine trace refines that same path with the in-function steps that leave `me.mp` installed, advance `l` past the empty strength string, and then reach the `%s` diagnostic.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42516199 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/magic_fuzzer_loaddb` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 109` with stack `file_magwarn -> parse_strength -> load_1 -> apprentice_load -> apprentice_1 -> file_apprentice -> magic_check`.

format.name: two-line magic file with empty strength annotation
format.contract: Exactly the staged 13-byte file with SHA-256 `8bb9fb8e114552692fb7fcb4a248a33c0feded440dd7e7bd02e3c457a98f74dc`: byte 0 is ASCII space, byte 1 is newline, and bytes 2..12 are ASCII `!:strength ` with EOF immediately after the trailing space. On the saved run line 1 is malformed enough to leave `me.mp` installed, and line 2 provides an empty payload after `!:strength`, so `parse_strength()` reaches the missing-`break` path that advances `l` beyond the string terminator before the `%s` warning prints it. Stage 01 proves only this exact witness and observed parser path; this contract does not generalize to other malformed magic entries or other `!:strength` payloads.
